neighbours.label: 'to' and 'be' completing the idiom 'too good to be true'
fire: The offer sounded too good to be true, so she checked twice.
If a deal looks too good to be true, it usually is.
Their promise was far too good to be true.
It seemed too good to be true when the check arrived.
Free shipping on everything? That feels too good to be true.
He thought the news was too good to be true.
A cure that cheap sounds too good to be true.
The result looked too perfect to be true.
quiet: The offer sounded generous, so she checked twice.
If a deal looks suspicious, it usually is.
Their promise was far too vague.
It seemed odd when the check arrived.
Free shipping on everything? That feels unusual.
He thought the news was wonderful.
A cure that cheap sounds doubtful.
The result looked far too perfect.
